name: Blackcurrant seed oil
short: Few safety data. Pooled arthritis trials of gamma-linolenic acid oils incl. this one: adverse events 20% vs 3% placebo, not significant. A pregnancy-infancy trial's authors called it well tolerated.
text: Few safety data on blackcurrant seed oil were found. In a randomised, double-blind trial in 313 pregnant women (151 assigned blackcurrant seed oil, 162 olive oil placebo), in which parental atopy was common (81.7%), making the infants at increased risk of atopy, the first doses were given at weeks 8 to 16 of pregnancy and continued until breastfeeding stopped, followed by supplementation of the infants until age 2; the authors reported that the supplement was well tolerated, but the abstract does not list adverse events. In a 24-week placebo-controlled trial in patients with active rheumatoid arthritis, no patients withdrew from blackcurrant seed oil because of adverse reactions, although many withdrew because of the 15 large capsules required daily. A Cochrane review that pooled rheumatoid arthritis trials of gamma-linolenic acid from evening primrose, borage or blackcurrant seed oil found adverse events in 20% with these oils versus 3% with placebo, a difference that was not statistically significant; the abstract does not give figures for blackcurrant seed oil alone. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
